description: Teach-mode + passive coaching during history. Educational only.

modules.title: Chest pain history structure
points: Characterize with OLDCARTS: onset, location, character, radiation, timing, exacerbating/relieving, severity.
Cardiac risk screen (exertional pattern, radiation, autonomic symptoms) takes priority before reflux/musculoskeletal causes.
Never anchor on a benign cause until ACS/PE/dissection red flags are excluded.

modules.title: Chest pain red flags
points: Hypotension, unequal breath sounds, or raised JVP with chest pain are unstable-until-proven-otherwise findings.
Escalate early rather than completing the full outpatient-style history first.

Q000065.why_ask: Character discriminates cardiac (pressure) from pleuritic/tearing causes.
Q000065.think: Pressure + exertional + radiation → treat as ACS until excluded.

Q000067.why_ask: Exertional relationship is one of the strongest bedside clues for ischaemic pain.
Q000067.think: Exertional pattern raises pre-test probability of ACS regardless of age.

Q000069.why_ask: Autonomic symptoms (sweating, nausea, sense of doom) often accompany ACS.
Q000069.think: Presence alongside chest pain strengthens cardiac concern even with an atypical description.

Q000038.why_ask: Syncope/near-syncope with chest pain suggests a haemodynamically significant cause.
Q000038.think: Combine with vitals — this is a stop-and-escalate combination.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: pressure/squeezing pattern
points: Treat as ischaemic until proven otherwise.
Obtain ECG and troponin pathway early.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: exertional pattern
points: Ask about prior similar exertional episodes (stable angina pattern).

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: tearing quality
points: Tearing/ripping pain radiating to the back raises aortic dissection concern.
Check for pulse/BP asymmetry between arms.
